question.problem: Find the second derivative of $f(t)=2{t}^{3}\,i-(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{t}^{2})\,j+(5{t}^{3}+\sqrt{5}t-2\sqrt{5})\,k$ with respect to $t.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the derivative of $f(t)$ by differentiating each component.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3})\,i-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{t}^{2})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5{t}^{3}+\sqrt{5}t-2\sqrt{5})\,k \\  & =6{t}^{2}\,i-(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t+2t)\,j+(15{t}^{2}+\sqrt{5})\,k \\  & =6{t}^{2}\,i+(\operatorname{sin}⁡t-2t)\,j+(15{t}^{2}+\sqrt{5})\,k\end{aligned}
$$

  

Then, we calculate ${f}^{″}(t)$ by differentiating ${f}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6{t}^{2})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t-2t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(15{t}^{2}+\sqrt{5})\,k \\  & =12t\,i+(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-2)\,j+30t\,k\end{aligned}
$$
